pieces.t: The Texas Journeyman Electrician examination is administered as an open book examination with approved reference rules. Open book testing allows candidates to use authorized materials during the exam, but it still requires serious preparation. A code book is only useful when the candidate understands how to locate information, read the rule correctly, and apply it within the time allowed. Open book electrical exams can be challenging because the NEC is large and detailed. Candidates who have not practiced reference navigation may spend too much time searching for answers. Strong preparation includes learning how to use the NEC index, article headings, definitions, tables, notes, exceptions, and related sections. A student should know how to turn a question into a searchable code topic and then apply the rule to the condition described.

pieces.t: Texas journeyman electrician candidates begin by registering and working as apprentice electricians under proper supervision. Apprentices should maintain accurate employment and experience records while gaining supervised electrical experience. Keeping organized documentation helps support the journeyman application when the candidate is ready to apply. The standard Texas Journeyman Electrician path requires at least 8,000 hours of on-the-job training under the supervision of a master electrician licensed in Texas. This experience is central to eligibility for the journeyman examination. Candidates should make sure their experience is properly documented and meets the TDLR requirements for the license classification. After meeting the experience requirement, the candidate submits the Journeyman Electrician license application to TDLR.

pieces.t: Texas requires electricians to be licensed through the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation. The Journeyman Electrician license is a statewide individual electrical license that authorizes journeyman-level electrical work within the scope of the license. Texas uses a statewide licensing structure rather than leaving journeyman electrician licensing entirely to local jurisdictions. To qualify for the Texas Journeyman Electrician license, an applicant must have at least 8,000 hours of on-the-job training under the supervision of a Texas licensed master electrician. This experience requirement supports the candidate’s eligibility to take the journeyman electrician examination. The Texas Journeyman Electrician license is different from a Residential Wireman license, Maintenance Electrician license, Master Electrician license, or Electrical Contractor license.

A journeyman electrician license is an individual trade license, while an electrical contractor license is a business-related credential connected to contracting activity. Texas also requires electrical apprentices to be registered while gaining qualifying experience. Apprentices should work under the proper supervision and keep clear records of their training, employment, and work experience. Accurate documentation helps avoid delays when applying for the journeyman license. License holders should also follow TDLR requirements for renewal, continuing education, and license maintenance. Continuing education helps electricians stay current with National Electrical Code updates, Texas law and rule changes, safe installation practices, and licensing responsibilities.

pieces.t: The Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation regulates electricians and electrical contractors in Texas. Electrical license holders must follow TDLR requirements, state laws, administrative rules, and the scope of work allowed by their license classification. The Texas Journeyman Electrician pathway requires supervised on-the-job training under a Texas-licensed Master Electrician. A candidate may apply to take the journeyman exam with at least 7,000 hours of qualifying training, but 8,000 hours are required before the Journeyman Electrician license can be issued. This structure allows eligible candidates to test before the final hours are completed while still requiring the full experience total for licensure. A Texas Journeyman Electrician license is different from a Texas Master Electrician license.

pieces.t: The master electrician path requires additional experience as a licensed journeyman before a candidate can qualify for the master-level examination. Candidates planning long-term advancement should understand how journeyman licensure fits into the progression toward master-level responsibility. Texas also requires license holders to maintain their licenses according to TDLR renewal and continuing education rules. pieces.t: Texas electrician licensing is handled through the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation. A Texas Journeyman Electrician is licensed to perform electrical work under the general supervision of a Texas licensed Master Electrician. With limited exemptions, anyone who performs electrical work in Texas must hold the proper electrical license for the work being performed. Texas electrician examinations are administered by PSI after TDLR approves the candidate’s eligibility. After the completed application has been reviewed and the required application fee has been received, the applicant is notified that they are approved to sit for the licensing examination. Candidates then schedule the examination through PSI.

pieces.t: Starting March 11, 2025, the Texas Journeyman Electrician written examination was changed to consist of two separate portions: an NEC Knowledge portion and a Calculations portion. Both portions are multiple choice, and candidates must pass each portion with a minimum score of 70%. Time remaining from one portion does not roll over into the next portion. The Texas Journeyman Electrician NEC Knowledge portion includes 59 items, including 3 non-scored items, with 130 minutes allowed. The Calculations portion includes 26 items, including 2 non-scored items, with 110 minutes allowed. The examination fee is listed as $78 for both portions, and a retake examination fee applies if a candidate fails one portion or both portions.

pieces.t: The Texas Journeyman Electrician exam is an open-book examination. Candidates are allowed to reference the National Electrical Code, 2023 Edition. Candidates are responsible for bringing their own NEC book to the examination site, and electronic notepads are provided. Texas has specific exam-room rules for reference materials. Any soft-bound edition of the 2023 National Electrical Code may be used for the examination. Loose-leaf, spiral-bound, and ring-bound copies of the NEC are not allowed in the examination room. The NEC book may be highlighted, underlined, and may contain notes before the examination session. NEC books may be tabbed with permanent index tabs manufactured or provided by the NEC book publisher. Candidates may not write, highlight, underline, index, or mark their NEC book during the examination session. Homemade, DIY, and non-NEC tabs are not allowed.

pieces.t: Texas journeyman electrician licensing begins with supervised electrical work experience. To apply for a Texas Journeyman Electrician license, an applicant must have completed at least 7,000 hours of on-the-job training under the supervision of a Master Electrician licensed in Texas. Submitting at least 7,000 hours allows the applicant to take the examination before reaching the full 8,000 hours required for licensure. The applicant must obtain verification from each Master Electrician who supervised the qualifying work. Experience must be documented and signed by each supervisor on the required Experience Verification Form. TDLR may contact individuals to verify the experience submitted with the application.

pieces.t: A typical Texas journeyman path includes registering and working in the electrical trade, gaining supervised on-the-job training under a Texas licensed Master Electrician, documenting qualifying hours, submitting the journeyman electrician license application, paying the required application fee, receiving examination approval, scheduling the PSI exam, passing both portions of the exam, reaching the full 8,000 hours required for licensure, and completing the remaining licensing steps through TDLR. Applicants must apply by mail for the initial journeyman electrician license application. The Texas Journeyman Electrician license application is submitted with the non-refundable application fee to the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation. Electrician licenses are valid for one year from the date of issuance and must be renewed annually.

pieces.t: Texas has statewide electrical licensing through the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation. Texas licenses electrical workers by classification, including apprentice electricians, journeyman electricians, master electricians, residential wiremen, maintenance electricians, journeyman industrial electricians, journeyman linemen, and sign electricians. This product is focused on the Texas Journeyman Electrician license. It also includes service entrance conductors as defined by the National Electrical Code.

pieces.t: To apply for a Texas Journeyman Electrician license, an applicant must have completed at least 7,000 hours of on-the-job training under the supervision of a Master Electrician licensed in Texas. The 7,000-hour threshold allows the applicant to take the examination before reaching the full 8,000 hours required for licensure. The examination is administered by PSI, and TDLR receives exam results electronically from the testing provider.

pieces.t: Texas electrician licensing is handled through the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation. The Texas Master Electrician examination is administered by PSI after the applicant’s eligibility has been approved by TDLR. The exam is designed to measure competency in master-level electrical knowledge, NEC application, and calculation skills. The Texas Master Electrician written examination consists of two separate multiple-choice portions: the NEC Knowledge Portion and the Calculations Portion. Time from one portion does not roll over into the other portion, so candidates should prepare for each section as its own timed exam event. The NEC Knowledge Portion is listed with 75 items, including 5 non-scored items, and 150 minutes of testing time.

pieces.t: The Texas electrician examinations are identified as open book examinations. For the current Texas exam reference rules, candidates are allowed to reference the National Electrical Code edition listed by TDLR and PSI for the examination. Candidates are responsible for bringing their own NEC book to the examination site. Texas reference rules are strict. The allowed NEC must be a soft-bound edition. Loose-leaf, spiralbound, or ring-bound copies are not allowed in the examination room. The NEC Handbook is not allowed. The NEC book may be highlighted, underlined, and may contain notes before the examination session. Candidates may not write, highlight, underline, index, or mark the NEC during the examination session. Texas also limits tabs. NEC books may be tabbed with permanent index tabs manufactured or provided by the NEC book publisher. Homemade, DIY, or non-NEC tabs are not permitted.

pieces.t: A practical Texas licensing path begins by confirming that the Master Electrician license is the correct license for the work and responsibility the candidate intends to perform. Texas requires a license for non-exempt electrical work, and electrical work must be performed through a licensed electrical contractor when required by law. To apply for a Texas Master Electrician license, the applicant must have held a Journeyman Electrician license for at least two years. TDLR notes that Journeyman Industrial Electrician experience may not be used to qualify for a Master Electrician license. The applicant must also show completion of 12,000 hours of on-the-job training under the supervision of a Master Electrician licensed in Texas. The applicant must obtain verification from each Master Electrician who supervised the qualifying work.

pieces.t: The Texas Master Electrician examination is administered by PSI for the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation. After TDLR receives and verifies the completed license application and experience documentation, the candidate receives notification of approval to take the licensing exam and may schedule testing through PSI. The Texas Master Electrician written examination consists of two portions : the NEC Knowledge Portion and the Calculations Portion . Both portions are multiple choice. Candidates must pass each portion with a minimum score of 70% . Time from one portion does not roll over into the other portion. The Texas Master Electrician NEC Knowledge Portion contains 75 items , including 5 non-scored items . Candidates are allowed 150 minutes , and a score of 70% correct is required to pass.

pieces.t: The Texas Master Electrician examination is an open book test . Candidates are allowed to reference the National Electrical Code during the examination and are responsible for bringing their own NEC book to the examination site. Electronic notepads are provided during the examination. A candidate’s NEC book may be highlighted, underlined, and may contain notes before the examination session. NEC books may be tabbed only with permanent index tabs manufactured or provided by the NEC book publisher.

pieces.t: The Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation regulates electrician licensing in Texas. With limited exemptions, anyone who performs electrical work in Texas must be licensed. Electrical work includes labor or material used in installing, maintaining, or extending electrical wiring systems and related appurtenances, apparatus, or equipment connected with the use of electrical energy, including service entrance conductors as defined by the National Electrical Code. A Texas Master Electrician is licensed to install, maintain, or extend electrical wiring systems and related appurtenances, apparatus, or equipment used in connection with electrical energy in, on, outside, or attached to buildings, residences, structures, property, or premises. This license represents an advanced individual credential in the Texas electrical licensing structure.

The applicant must also show completion of at least 12,000 hours of on-the-job training under the supervision of a Texas-licensed Master Electrician. Each supervising Master Electrician must verify the applicant’s experience. If the applicant held a municipal or regional master electrician license, the applicant may verify their own on-the-job training for the years they held that license. This course follows the International Code Council (ICC) guidelines and focuses on structural framing, general building design, and code-compliant construction practices for residential and light commercial projects up to three stories. Designed for flexible study, the course aligns with ICC examination objectives and provides targeted instruction for contractors pursuing national certification through the ICC credentialing framework.

pieces.t: For Georgia candidates, the Journeyman Plumber examination is delivered by computer at PSI test centers. The PSI candidate information bulletin describes the Georgia Journeyman exam as follows: Total time: 5 hours to complete the Journeyman examination. Two-part format: 2.5 hours for Part 1, then a break, followed by 2.5 hours for Part 2. Question set: 100 scored test questions plus 20 additional pretest questions (120 total questions presented). Passing standard: Scores are reported as a final scaled score; a final scaled score of 70 is required to pass. That structure matters for your study plan. pieces.t: This package is designed for an open book testing environment where code lookups are part of the exam strategy. In Georgia, the journeyman reference materials may be used during the examination, while the bulletin notes that reference materials may not be used for the other plumbing exams. The most effective open-book strategy is built around three skills: Recognition: identify what the question is really asking (definitions, sizing, materials, installation requirements, prohibited practices, or exceptions). Location: quickly determine where that topic lives in the code (chapter, section, table, or the index). Confirmation: verify the requirement in the exact code language, including any exceptions, footnotes, or related provisions. The IPC is dense by design. Using it well is a learned skill.

pieces.t: Your study is most effective when you combine “know it” learning with “find it” practice. Journeyman plumbing exams are built around real-world plumbing knowledge and code-based decision-making, which means you’ll typically face questions that test your ability to: Interpret code requirements correctly: understand what is required, what is permitted, and what is prohibited. Work through water supply topics: distribution concepts, fixture supply expectations, and code-driven provisions that impact installation. Apply fixture and installation standards: practical compliance choices that match the intent of the code. Use definitions and exceptions effectively: many questions hinge on a definition, a key term, or an exception that changes how a rule applies.

pieces.t: To build speed for an open-book environment, practice with a simple routine: Daily navigation drills (10–20 minutes): choose a topic and locate 10 related code sections using the index and table of contents, then summarize the rule in one sentence. Weak-area rotation: focus on the chapters where you lose time—then repeat them until your search process speeds up. Question-to-code mapping: after each practice set, write down which IPC chapter/section answered each question. This builds your mental “map” of the book. pieces.t: The NASCLA Accredited Trade Examination for Electrical Contractors is intended for individuals performing, supervising, or qualifying electrical contracting work. It evaluates knowledge related to the installation, maintenance, repair, management, and safe operation of electrical systems in accordance with applicable codes and standards. The examination contains 100 scored questions. Candidates must answer at least 75 scored questions correctly to meet the minimum passing standard. The examination allows 270 minutes, which provides four hours and thirty minutes to complete the test. Ten additional non-scored experimental questions may also be administered. These questions are used for future examination development and do not count toward the final score.

This course focuses on the structure and enforcement of the International Plumbing Code, covering fixture requirements, water distribution, sanitary drainage, vent systems, and health safeguards as defined by the IPC. Designed for plumbers, inspectors, and contractors pursuing licensing or certification, it emphasizes code interpretation, cross-references with local amendments, and exam-oriented practice questions. The IPC content supports state and county-level plumbing license exams and is a core reference for continuing education in plumbing systems and construction code compliance. This course includes the following modules:

pieces.h: About Online Practice Exam for Code of Federal Regulations, (OSHA) 29 Part 1926
pieces.t: The ONLINE PRACTICE EXAM FOR CODE OF FEDERAL REGULATIONS, (OSHA) 29 PART 1926, offered by 1 Exam Prep, provides structured test preparation aligned with the U.S. Department of Labor’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) standards for construction safety and health. This 2019 edition covers regulatory content from Title 29 CFR Part 1926, focusing on compliance for construction site safety management, worker protection protocols, and hazard control procedures. Candidates use this online exam to assess readiness for OSHA-based qualification assessments and contractor licensing exams, integrating federal safety regulations, subpart reviews, and procedural updates. The exam serves individuals seeking certification or continuing education in construction safety compliance, reinforcing key federal mandates essential for contractors, builders, and site supervisors nationwide.

pieces.t: The Texas Journeyman Electrician exam is administered in two separate portions : an NEC Knowledge portion and a Calculations portion. Both portions are multiple-choice, and you must pass each portion with the required score to move forward. NEC Knowledge Portion: 59 items (including non-scored items) with a set time limit. Calculations Portion: Administered as a separate portion with its own time limit. Passing requirement: Each portion requires the minimum passing score. Testing fee: The bulletin lists an exam fee for both portions together, with retake fees applying if you need to retest. This guide supports both portions by pairing code-based question practice with calculation-focused review so you can prepare in the same way you’ll be tested.

pieces.t: Licensing can feel confusing because there’s the exam, the paperwork, and the timing. While every applicant’s situation is different, the general path to testing and licensing in Texas follows a clear structure. Complete your license application: Submit the required application to the Texas licensing authority for electricians. Receive exam approval: Once your application is reviewed and the application fee is received, you’ll be notified that you’re approved to sit for the exam. Schedule your exam appointment: Texas delivers electrician exams through a third-party testing vendor with multiple locations across the state. Prepare your test-day materials: Bring required identification, and if using the NEC for the open-book portion, ensure your book format and materials are compliant.

pieces.t: Refrigeration Principles: Review the basic refrigeration cycle and the relationship between compression, condensation, expansion, and evaporation. Understand sensible heat, latent heat, saturation, pressure-temperature relationships, superheat, and subcooling. Compressors: Study common compressor types, operation, electrical requirements, lubrication, capacity, failure conditions, and troubleshooting. The compressor is a central component of both air-conditioning and refrigeration systems. Evaporators and Condensers: Understand heat absorption at the evaporator and heat rejection at the condenser. Review airflow, temperature differences, refrigerant conditions, coil cleanliness, and common performance problems. Metering Devices: Review thermostatic expansion valves, fixed metering devices, and other methods used to regulate refrigerant entering an evaporator.

pieces.t: The ICC Code Enforcement Officer exam is identified as CE-O . ICC lists the exam with 50 questions and a 2.5-hour duration . The ICC Code Enforcement Program describes the Code Enforcement Officer role as a field professional who helps foster safe, healthy, and attractive communities by working with residents, property owners, and business owners to achieve compliance through education, inspection, mediation, and formal enforcement action. ICC’s current Code Enforcement Program also states that completion of the Code Enforcement Technician credential is a prerequisite for the Code Enforcement Officer credential. Candidates preparing for the CE-O exam should make sure their ICC credential path is complete and that they follow the registration instructions in their myICC account.

pieces.t: Texas Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Contractor licensing is administered by TDLR under Texas Occupations Code Chapter 1302 and Texas Administrative Code Chapter 75 . A Class A license allows the license holder to work on systems of any size within the authorized endorsement. Unlike Class B, Class A does not impose the Class B cooling-capacity and heating-output limitations. The Commercial Refrigeration endorsement covers the use of mechanical or absorption equipment to control temperature or humidity to satisfy the intended use of a specific space. Commercial refrigeration and qualifying process cooling and heating work include equipment such as coolers, freezers, ice machines, and equipment used for applicable temperature and humidity control.

pieces.t: The Texas Journeyman Electrician examination is an open book test . The approved technical reference is the National Electrical Code, NEC, 2026 Edition . Candidates are responsible for bringing an acceptable NEC book to the examination site. Soft-bound editions of the NEC may be used. Loose-leaf, spiral-bound, and ring-bound copies are not permitted. The NEC Handbook is also not permitted as the examination-room reference. Candidates may not add new notes, highlighting, underlining, indexing, or other markings during the testing session. The included rental copy of the 2026 NEC is highlighted and tabbed to support preparation. Candidates should use the book during the full 6 months of course access so that major sections become familiar before exam day.

pieces.t: The standard Texas Journeyman Electrician pathway requires a total of 8,000 hours of qualifying on-the-job training under the supervision of a Texas-licensed Master Electrician. An applicant may submit at least 7,000 hours to become eligible to take the examination before completing the final 1,000 hours required for licensing. Qualifying electrical experience must be documented by the Master Electrician or Master Electricians who supervised the work. The experience documentation is submitted as part of the TDLR application process. Texas also recognizes approved education pathways that may affect how candidates qualify for the Journeyman Electrician examination. Applicants using an approved educational pathway must meet the requirements applicable to that program. A Texas Journeyman Electrician performs electrical work under the general supervision of a Master Electrician .

pieces.t: The Texas Journeyman Industrial Electrician license is a specialized electrical credential with a limited industrial scope. pieces.h: About Texas Journeyman Industrial Electrician Book Package
pieces.t: Prepare for the Texas Journeyman Industrial Electrician examination with the National Electrical Code, NEC, 2026 Edition , the current electrical code reference used for Texas electrician examinations. Texas adopted the 2026 National Electrical Code effective September 1, 2026, making this edition the primary technical reference for candidates pursuing the Texas Journeyman Industrial Electrician license through the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation. The Texas Journeyman Industrial Electrician license is a specialized electrical credential for individuals performing electrical work exclusively at qualifying industrial businesses. The license applies to electrical work at facilities such as chemical plants, petrochemical plants, refineries, natural gas plants, natural gas treating plants, pipelines, and oil and gas exploration and production operations.

pieces.t: The Texas Journeyman Industrial Electrician examination is an open book test . The current approved technical reference is the National Electrical Code, NEC, 2026 Edition . Candidates are responsible for bringing their own acceptable NEC book to the examination site. Any soft-bound edition of the NEC may be used. Candidates may not write, highlight, underline, index, or otherwise mark the NEC during the examination. Homemade, do-it-yourself, or non-NEC tabs are not permitted. Additional loose paper or pages attached to the book are also prohibited.

Required continuing education addresses the National Electrical Code, Texas electrician law, Texas electrician administrative rules, and electrical safety. pieces.t: The Texas Journeyman Lineman Electrician license is a specialized credential covering electrical work on transmission and distribution systems from the original source of electricity to the substation. Texas provides qualifying experience pathways for applicants seeking this license. One pathway is completion of at least 7,000 hours of training in an apprenticeship program approved by the United States Department of Labor . Another pathway is at least 3.5 years of experience as a Journeyman Lineman for an electric utility, electric cooperative, municipally owned utility, or electrical contractor in Texas. Applicants must provide documentation supporting the pathway used to qualify. TDLR reviews the information as part of the licensing process before examination authorization is granted.

pieces.t: The Texas Journeyman Lineman Electrician credential is a specialized electrical license with a defined scope. It applies to electrical work associated with transmission and distribution systems from the original source of electricity to a substation for further distribution. One qualification pathway requires at least 7,000 hours of training in a Journeyman Lineman apprenticeship program approved by the United States Department of Labor . Texas also provides an alternative experience pathway. Applicants may qualify with at least 3.5 years of experience as a Journeyman Lineman for an electric utility, electric cooperative, municipally owned utility, or electrical contractor in Texas. The Journeyman Lineman Electrician credential is not a general-purpose Journeyman Electrician license. Its authorized work is limited to the transmission and distribution scope established for the credential.

pieces.t: A Texas Journeyman Sign Electrician is licensed to perform electrical sign work under the general supervision of a Master Electrician or Master Sign Electrician . Applicants must document at least 8,000 hours of on-the-job training under a Texas-licensed Master Electrician or Master Sign Electrician. The experience submitted with the application must be properly verified. TDLR reviews the documentation before authorizing eligible applicants to take the examination. The Journeyman Sign Electrician credential is a specialized electrical license. It focuses on electrical sign work rather than the broader electrical scope associated with the Texas Journeyman Electrician license. Electrical sign work can involve the installation, alteration, servicing, and maintenance of electrical signs and outline lighting systems within the scope established for the credential.

pieces.t: Definitions, Theory, and Plans: Review Article 100 definitions, electrical theory, plan interpretation, conductor properties, voltage, current, resistance, power, and the terminology used throughout the NEC. Services: Services are heavily represented in both examination portions. Study Article 230, service conductors, service equipment, disconnecting means, service ratings, grounding, bonding, and available service configurations. Separately Derived Systems: Review transformers, grounding and bonding of separately derived systems, system bonding jumpers, grounding electrode conductors, and related Article 250 requirements. Feeders: Study Article 215 requirements, feeder conductor sizing, ampacity, overcurrent protection, grounding and bonding, neutral calculations, and feeder demand calculations. Branch Circuits: Branch-circuit conductors are one of the largest NEC Knowledge categories.

pieces.t: A Texas Master Electrician is licensed to perform electrical work within the scope established by Texas law. This credential represents an advanced level of individual electrician licensing and carries responsibilities beyond those of the Journeyman Electrician. The Texas Master Electrician license is an individual credential.

pieces.t: A Texas Residential Wireman is licensed to perform electrical installations in single-family and multifamily dwellings not exceeding four stories . Applicants may qualify by providing proof of completion of an approved career and technology education program or by documenting at least 4,000 hours of on-the-job electrical training under the supervision of a Texas-licensed Master Electrician or Residential Wireman. Applicants using the experience pathway must obtain verification from each Master Electrician or Residential Wireman who supervised the qualifying work. TDLR may contact the individuals involved to verify submitted experience. Completion of an approved career and technology education program does not eliminate the examination requirement. Candidates using that pathway must still take and pass the Texas Residential Wireman examination.

pieces.t: The standard Texas Tradesman Plumber-Limited examination pathway requires applicants to be registered as a Plumber's Apprentice in Texas and to have at least 4,000 hours of qualifying plumbing experience . Applicants must also complete a 24-hour TSBPE-approved training program unless they qualify for an exemption. The training program includes continuing professional education, OSHA construction-industry safety training, and instruction involving the International Residential Code and/or Uniform Plumbing Code. Applicants enrolled in or having completed an apprenticeship program approved by the United States Department of Labor Office of Apprenticeship may qualify under an alternative training pathway. Certain holders of current out-of-state Journeyman or Master Plumber licenses may also be exempt from the 24-hour training requirement.

pieces.t: A Texas Master Electrician is an individually licensed electrical professional. Applicants must have held a Texas Journeyman Electrician license for at least two years and must document at least 12,000 hours of on-the-job training under the supervision of a Texas-licensed Master Electrician . Qualifying experience must be verified as part of the state application process. Journeyman Industrial Electrician experience does not count toward the experience requirement for the Texas Master Electrician credential. The Texas Master Electrician license and the Texas Electrical Contractor license are not the same credential. The Master Electrician license applies to the individual. The Electrical Contractor license applies to the contracting business. A Texas electrical contracting business must have a licensed Master Electrician serving as its Master Electrician of Record .

pieces.t: The Texas Residential Wireman license is an individual electrician credential designed for residential electrical work within its defined scope. A Residential Wireman may perform qualifying electrical installations in single-family and multifamily dwellings not exceeding four stories . Under the standard experience pathway, applicants must document at least 4,000 hours of qualifying on-the-job electrical training . Texas also provides an approved career and technical education pathway that may apply to qualifying candidates. The Residential Wireman license is more limited in scope than the Texas Journeyman Electrician license. Candidates should understand that earning the Residential Wireman credential does not automatically provide authority to perform every type of commercial, industrial, or unrestricted electrical installation.
